chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā from Muhammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Yaqṭīnī said:

Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) sent me a bundle of garments, servants, and a pilgrimage offering for me, a pilgrimage offering for my brother Mūsā ibn ʿUbayd, and a pilgrimage offering for Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and ordered us to perform Hajj on his behalf. There was one hundred dinars among us, divided into three parts. When I intended to pack the garments, I saw clay in the folds of the garments. I said to the messenger, 'What is this?' He said, 'No baggage is sent except that clay from the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is placed in it.' Then the messenger said, 'Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) said: It is a guarantee of safety, by God's permission.'

He ordered us regarding the money to do various things: to give to his Ahl al-Bayt and to needy people who are disregarded. He ordered that three hundred dinars be paid to Ruḥm, a woman who was his, and ordered me to divorce her on his behalf and to provide her with maintenance (mutʿah) from this money. He ordered me to witness her divorce with Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā and another person whose name Muhammad ibn ʿĪsā forgot.

All the figurative expressions of divorce (kinayah) are not considered valid from the man's saying 'You are free/clear' or 'Your cord is on your shoulder' and whatever runs in its manner. We have clarified that in what preceded, and what follows will add to its clarification, as he narrated:

key_terms.أَضْعَافُ الثِّيَابِ: The folds or layers of the garments
key_terms.أُمَتِّعَهَا: To provide her with maintenance (mut'ah) upon divorce
key_terms.بَرِيَّةٌ: A figurative term for divorce meaning 'exempt/clear'
key_terms.حَبْلُكِ عَلَى غَارِبِكِ: A figurative idiom for divorce meaning 'your affair is in your hands'
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ: A pilgrimage offering or funds for Hajj
key_terms.خَلِيَّةٌ: A figurative term for divorce meaning 'free/clear'
key_terms.رُحْمَ: A proper name of a woman
key_terms.رِزَمَ: A bundle or package of goods
key_terms.صِلَةُ: Kinship ties or charitable giving to family
key_terms.طِينٌ: Clay, specifically from the grave of al-Husayn

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of clay from the grave of al-Husayn in gifts sent by the Imams, and what are the rules for figurative divorce (kinayah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual significance of clay from the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) as a divine amulet for safety during travel, reflecting Shia devotional practices. It further elucidates the jurisprudential principle that figurative divorce expressions (kunya) are not considered valid unless explicitly intended, emphasizing the need for clarity in marital dissolution. The narrative also underscores the Imam’s attention to financial justice, including specific maintenance payments and the appointment of witnesses for divorce proceedings.
